title: Robot identity bootstrap workflow: gated creation, attestation, and audit hooks
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
Introduce a gated, auditable machine/robot identity bootstrap workflow for service accounts that enforces least-privilege templates, ownership assignment, and periodic attestation. This ticket covers the end-to-end flow: request surface (GitHub PR or Console), automated template selection, approval gating, ephemeral credential issuance, audit-log hooks, and SSO/SAML group mapping for RBAC v2 compatibility. The goal is to reduce manual onboarding, eliminate over-permissive defaults, and make ownership traceable for compliance audits.

Background & motivation:
Current creation flows allow engineers and some admins to call internal APIs to create service accounts. Over time we see many long-lived accounts with broad scopes and unclear owners. Incidents and internal audits highlight two recurring issues: (1) accounts drift to excess privileges and (2) ownership is stale or unknown. RBAC v2 introduces role bindings and SSO group mappings — we need a creation workflow that pushes best-practice templates and ties each account to an owner and an audit trail.

Scope / non-goals:
- In-scope: request UI (Console + GitHub PR template), server-side gating service ("svc-bootstrap"), least-privilege template registry, approval workflow (can be automated), ephemeral credential issuance (short-lived keys or OIDC exchange), periodic ownership attestation webhook, audit-log integration with SIEM, SSO/SAML group mapping push for RBAC v2.
- Out-of-scope: wholesale migration of existing service accounts (separate migration program), key rotation automation for third-party integrations (follow-up).

Acceptance criteria:
- Engineers can create a service account via (A) a standardized GitHub PR template or (B) Console guided flow that selects an appropriate least-privilege template.
- Creation requests are evaluated by svc-bootstrap which returns either: auto-approved (meets template & requester policy), requires 1 approver (for elevated scopes), or blocked (violates policy).
- On approval, the system issues ephemeral credentials (OIDC token exchange + optional short-lived key) and writes a structured audit event to central logging (index: redwood-svc-accounts) with owner, template, justification, and request_id.
- The account is assigned a canonical owner (user or team) with a TTL-driven attestation schedule (default 90 days). If an attestation window lapses without confirmation, the account is locked and listed for cleanup.
- RBAC v2 role bindings are created as minimal as possible; SSO/SAML group mapping is written to the mapping table for downstream enforcement.
- Console surface shows creation request history, owner, last attestation date, and a one-click revoke/rotate action.

Design decisions & trade-offs:
1) Templates vs free-form scopes: Templates reduce variance and are required for self-serve. Allow a "custom" path but require explicit approver and justification to avoid sprawl.
2) Ephemeral creds: Prefer OIDC short-lived tokens where the consumer supports it. Fallback to short-lived keys (24h) for legacy integrations. This reduces blast radius but adds complexity to consumers — we will publish migration docs.
3) Auto-approve heuristics: For low-risk templates and requesters in an allowed group (e.g., platform-engineering), auto-approve to keep throughput. For risky templates, require manual approval to balance security and developer velocity.
4) Audit volume: Every lifecycle event emits structured JSON to the SIEM. We will sample debug-level events but keep critical lifecycle events (create/approve/attest/revoke) always logged.

Implementation plan (high-level):
- Week 1: Build svc-bootstrap microservice skeleton, template registry schema, and GitHub PR template. (ENG-76421-A)
- Week 2: Implement approval rules engine, Console request UI wireframe, and initial SSO mapping API. (ENG-76421-B)
- Week 3: Integrate ephemeral credential issuer (OIDC flow) and key fallback, produce audit event to dev SIEM index. (ENG-76421-C)
- Week 4: Attestation scheduler, lock/cleanup path, Console owner UI, tests, and docs. (ENG-76421-D)
- Week 5: Internal dogfood + security review, telemetry, and rollout plan. (ENG-76421-E)

Telemetry & observability:
- Metrics: creation_requests_total, auto_approvals_total, manual_approvals_total, failed_creations_total, attestation_missed_total, ephemeral_issuances_total.
- Logging: structured audit events include: request_id, template_id, requester_id, owner_id, approver_ids, justification, decision, and timestamp.
- Dashboards: create a Console dashboard for pending attestations and accounts locked-by-policy. Link: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/sa-lifecycle

Security & compliance notes:
- All creation actions require an authenticated identity; Console flows use SSO SAML assertions and GitHub flows require verified commit authorship.
- Audit events are immutable and forwarded to long-term retention for compliance.
- Security review required before roll-out (subtask created).

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Developer friction from mandatory templates -> Mitigation: create low-friction templates and an escape hatch for emergency service accounts with short TTLs and mandatory post-hoc review.
- Risk: Legacy consumers fail with ephemeral creds -> Mitigation: provide a 60-day migration window and short-lived key fallback with monitored usage.
- Risk: Approval bottleneck -> Mitigation: automating approvals for low-risk cases and provide a Slack/Console notification for pending approvals to reduce latency.

Open questions (to decide in kickoff):
- What is the canonical owner model: single user vs team alias? (preference: team alias with optional primary user).
- Default attestation cadence: 90 vs 180 days? (default 90, configurable per template).
- Approved approver scopes: should platform-admins be able to sign off on any template? (likely yes, but track approvals).

References & artifacts:
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SEC/Service+Account+Lifecycle+Project (draft spec)
- GitHub PR prototype: https://github.com/redwood-internal/svc-bootstrap/pull/12 (prototype endpoint + schema)
- Compliance ticket: ENG-74211 (audit retention & SIEM mapping)

Next steps (this sprint):
- Kickoff meeting with Security, Platform, and Console: schedule week of 2025-01-20.
- Create svc-bootstrap repo, push PR with API contract and schema.
- Draft Console mockups and GitHub PR template and run quick user interview with 3 engineers.
